100.title: A Bar at the Folies-Bergère
100.why: One layer is recorded, one layer is invented. Manet divides reality between the figure facing us in front of the counter and her impossible reflection in the glass behind her, where an observer approaches her from another angle. Two Layers operates on that exact threshold: a Bangkok architect in 2026 suspecting his world is rendered, and an archivist in 3026 re-entering the simulation to sit near him.

flooddash-fb.title: The Reading of the Bulletin of the Grande Armée
flooddash-fb.why: The household and neighbours gathered close around the posted official bulletin: 112,000 citizens reading the same daily flood situation briefing in Thai — verified public data today, safer tomorrow.

nst.title: Nang Talung: Hanuman, General of the Monkey Army
nst.why: The shadow puppet of Nakhon Si Thammarat cut from treated hide: Khao Luang and Pak Phanang basin, ancient Tambralinga, and thirty-plus civic feeds brought to light through silhouette and precision.
nst.medium: carved and painted cowhide shadow puppet

phuket.title: The Royal Fleet Procession
phuket.why: Siamese royal fleet moving across open water, each vessel holding its exact position in formation: thirty-four Andaman feeds — maritime corridors, tourism vessels, weather, and safety — coordinated into one operational picture.
phuket.medium: tempera and gold leaf on cloth

hcmc.title: Boulevard Montmartre, Spring
hcmc.why: Traffic cameras, flood sensors, air readings and the news wire, held in one frame — the city seen from above so a route can be chosen, not merely watched.

lopburi.title: Wooded Landscape with Watermill
lopburi.why: A mill is a control point on the water: the Pa Sak Jolasid reservoir, the basin feed, the camera grid and the social feed all meet at one gate, and the level there decides the release.

mtt.title: The Fight Between Carnival and Lent
mtt.why: A whole district square taken over by one event — arena, halls, car park, flood gauge and air reading stacked on one map, so the operator can see where the load actually is.

kuching.title: The Mérode Altarpiece (The Annunciation Triptych)
kuching.why: One desk holding every domain at once: the letter, the goods, the weather outside the window and the trap on the sill. Currency, flights, imagery and environment read together, not in separate rooms.

malaysia.title: Panoramic Landscape along the Rhine
malaysia.why: Every basin, every route, every person who lives far from help, on one map — the whole country read at a glance, in three languages.

chula.title: The School of Athens
chula.why: The academy gathered under one vaulted geometry — philosophers, geometers, astronomers, and architects: forty-seven campus feeds unified under one roof for Siam's premier university.

chonburi.title: The Coalmen (Les Déchargeurs de charbon)
chonburi.why: Industrial river barges, mechanical planks, and continuous freight hauling beneath the transit bridge: Eastern Seaboard industrial logistics, heavy petrochemical corridors, and manufacturing flows tracked without pause.

kmitl.title: Astronomical Observations: Jupiter
kmitl.why: A nocturnal observatory peering through optical telemetry into planetary orbits: Ladkrabang's aerospace, engineering towers, satellite telemetry, and signal grid monitored through the night.

air-dnd.title: Rue Halévy, Viewed from a Seventh-Floor Window
air-dnd.why: Rain crossing a city: the washout condition the forecast is built on — CAMS minus rain over ground PM2.5, three days out, with the five provinces most at risk named first.

asiawatch.title: Kunyu Wanguo Quantu (Complete Map of All the Nations of the World)
asiawatch.why: The world drawn from the other side of the Pacific: Southeast, East and South Asia, Thailand, and the Gulf as the energy lifeline, watched from inside the region rather than appended to it.

worldconsole.title: Typus Aspectuum Oppositionum et Coniunctionum in Planetis
worldconsole.why: The entire world on one engraved plate, every coordinate visible at once: aircraft and ships worldwide, conflict and fire hotspots, and the market strip docked open beside it.

mem.title: The Iron Rolling Mill (Modern Cyclopes)
mem.why: The dispatch read at the end of the shift: multi-source feeds with no editorial layer, the signal arriving before anybody has had time to interpret it.

daytraders.artist: Thomas Rowlandson and Augustus Charles Pugin
daytraders.title: The New Stock Exchange, from The Microcosm of London, Volume 3
daytraders.why: The exchange floor where every price is set by eye and voice in the same room — SET and MAI, US markets and Thai ESG, read against the Graham, Buffett and Munger frameworks.

formhypes.title: The Baptism of Christ
formhypes.why: A form taken apart into the numbers that make it: eleven profiles from rectilinear to pinwheel, nine metrics — rent, area, sky reach, daylight, distinctiveness — recalculated on every edit.

phuket-bus.title: Omnibus
phuket-bus.why: Passengers in an omnibus moving through the city, watching the street through the glass: real-time GPS telemetry, rider mobile view, and the exact second the next municipal bus pulls up to the curb.

scth.title: Village Festival
scth.why: A whole town reporting at once: complaints arriving by Telegram and LINE, classified and laid over the map, so one pattern becomes one task for somebody to answer.

nsp.title: The Apotheosis of Henry IV and the Proclamation of the Regency of Marie de Médicis
nsp.why: One proclamation carried out across a nation: twenty-one channels, a programme guide, and CAP v1.2 alerts that reach every screen in the country at the same moment.

carbon.title: The Hay Wain
carbon.why: The standing stock, counted: carbon in the trees, removals, emissions, fire and fossil CO₂ — every figure with its source and its uncertainty attached, province by province.

techhunt.title: Nighthawks
techhunt.why: The late-night diner on the corner where founders and nocturnal builders gather: 125 verified startups across seven domains hunted down and ranked by live market signal.

tkcx.title: The Battle of San Romano
tkcx.why: A formation executed on a plan: the same move made three times from three benches. Team assembly is a strategy problem, so it is solved as one — under a salary cap.

ikigai.title: Vanitas with Violin and Glass Ball
ikigai.why: The balance sheet read as signal: cash runway, a bank scorecard and a composite index — and the sand in the glass, because runway is the number that decides how long you have.

ladder.title: The Moneychangers
ladder.why: Weighing the deal before it is weighed by anyone else: the scorecard, the checklist and the thesis match, all read in one room at one table.

omniarcade.title: Wrestlers
omniarcade.collection: Los Angeles County Museum of Art
omniarcade.why: A drill, not a game: two bodies, one move, repeated until it is learned — every cartridge carries a briefing on the skill it trains and the limit of the claim.

ekkasarn.title: Scholar at his Desk
ekkasarn.why: A scholar at his desk with the document open in front of him: invoices, receipts and certificates read, sorted by type and pulled apart into fields — no login, nothing filed.

nonscrape.title: The Bookworm
nonscrape.why: One page, one reader, one answer: hand it a URL and a question and it reads the page in its own language, then returns the answer with its citations attached.

luma-house.title: Interior of the Buurkerk, Utrecht
luma-house.why: A room whose daylight is the subject and whose geometry is the calculation: sunlit floor area and heat gain computed on the plan before a single picture is generated.

champion.title: Les Joueurs de football (Football Players)
champion.why: The board from above: players reduced to intersecting planes, every position a choice the others depend on — and the match answering immediately when the plan is set.

soccer.title: The Football Players
soccer.collection: Solomon R. Guggenheim Museum, New York
soccer.why: Players in striped jerseys passing and contesting space in dynamic rhythm: tactics desk, squad movements, and real-time match geometry laid out on one pitch.

vision.title: Self-Portrait in a Convex Mirror
vision.why: A picture that means one thing head-on and another from the side: the same pixels, read by a model at a different angle, become edges, then motion, then a guess.

luggage-tag.title: Trompe l’œil: Letter Rack with Writing Instruments
luggage-tag.why: A plain board and a written label, and nothing else: ground, ink, four ranks and one optional colour — with an audit that fails the build if the tag carries anything it should not.

superleague.title: Portrait of the Artist’s Sisters Playing Chess
superleague.why: Two players, one board, one move at a time: the league is turn-based so the next decision is never made for you — pass, or hold the shape.

simcity.title: Brooklyn Bridge
simcity.collection: Yale University Art Gallery, New Haven
simcity.why: The steel lattice, glowing cables, and soaring infrastructure of a modern metropolis: real-site urban economics simulated block by block on OpenStreetMap.

iaas.title: The Courtyard of a House in Delft
iaas.why: The work happens in the client's courtyard, under the client's rules, with the client in the room — one problem they already have, built small and cheap on data they already hold.

probono.title: Banquet of the Officers of the St George Civic Guard
probono.why: An institution's own people, in their own hall, doing the job the city hired them for: five platforms built with the body that has to use them, and kept by them.

stages.title: Cicero Denounces Catiline
stages.why: The work demonstrated to the room that has to decide: five stages across Asia in 2026, each with a system running live, not a slide about one.

non.title: Self-Portrait
non.why: Anthropologist, architect, builder: the work starts by watching how a city actually behaves, then turning what was seen into an interface nobody needs a manual for.

poon.title: Self-Portrait
poon.why: Infrastructure, policy, and execution held to the city: a master plan co-authored, a bus predicted, and a country read as what it is — a complex adaptive system that has to keep working.

collective.title: The Raft of the Medusa
collective.why: A crew assembled for one voyage out of people who did not know each other before: specialists who join for the mission in front of them, not for a place on an org chart.

press.title: The Uprising
press.why: Outside the room, the work is on the street: the same argument, shown in public, to people who never sat in the meeting.

entity.title: The Moneylender and his Wife
entity.why: A registered business, written down: one registration number, one date, one jurisdiction, one address and one capital — the particulars that let a client check who they are contracting.

standards.title: The Ghent Altarpiece (open)
standards.why: The standard set by the workshop that did the work, not by a committee: two brothers, thousands of hours, and the result hung as the measure of the trade.

ledger.title: The Large Piece of Turf
ledger.why: One specimen, measured, dated and signed: the record made as you work, with its source and its age attached — the ledger that survives after the screen is gone.

brief.title: The Choice of Hercules
brief.why: The moment the decision is made: not a study of the problem, but a choice of the one thing worth building — two weeks, your data, one screen somebody can actually use.

plates.title: The Gallery of Cornelis van der Geest
plates.why: A cabinet of the world's pictures, each one labelled with where it came from: this book works the same way — one picture per system, and the credit printed underneath it.

colophon.title: Saint Anthony Tormented by Demons
colophon.why: The maker's mark cut into the block: this book was built by hand, from public sources, with every plate carrying its licence — the colophon is the receipt.

flood-ami.title: Under the Wave off Kanagawa (The Great Wave)
flood-ami.why: Nine sources — NASA FIRMS, GISTDA, CEMS, HIMAWARI-9, TMD, Open-Meteo, OSM, tide stations — folded into one picture, refreshed every 3–60 minutes. Seventy-seven provinces reading the same wave.

sikhio.title: Effects of Good Government in the City
sikhio.why: Every trade in a well-run town has its place and its hour: AQI, weather, traffic and the people they act on, arranged so a municipality can read its own pulse.

lcbcity.title: Men of the Docks
lcbcity.why: Stevedores, heavy freight, and massive ocean-going hulls on the industrial waterfront: Laem Chabang's port corridors, lorry GPS telemetry, and container dwell times read as one working dock.

yala.title: View of Delft
yala.why: A provincial town held still and legible: a 3D model, satellite layers, flood watch and Deep South incident feeds, read without hurry because nothing is moving.

city-hub.title: Broadway Boogie Woogie
city-hub.collection: Museum of Modern Art, New York
city-hub.why: Type a city's name and get its grid: the same street lattice, the same lenses, five cities running side by side. The comparison is the product.

bkk-atlas.title: The Tower of Babel
bkk-atlas.why: 432,077 buildings, extruded one by one — terrain, canals, the BTS lines, Treasury land prices and rain radar layered on top of a city that actually exists.

bkk-culture.title: Ramakien Murals at Wat Phra Kaew
bkk-culture.collection: Wat Phra Kaew, Grand Palace, Bangkok
bkk-culture.why: Nine historical quarters, 571 registered cultural monuments and seven curated walks: heritage lived continuously across sacred architecture, royal murals, and surrounding city streets.

jakarta.title: Wanderer above the Sea of Fog
jakarta.why: The operator above the model: massing and terrain from OSM, bulletins from BMKG, incident reports from citizens, flood-risk zones from the city — Indonesian and English on one desk.

slic.title: Composition VII
slic.why: Five pillars and 157 cities in one composition. The weights belong to the reader: change them and the ranking changes with them.

globalmonitor.title: World map (Nova et Aucta Orbis Terrae Descriptio)
globalmonitor.why: Four theatres on one sheet, the world flattened so it can be acted on: aircraft, ships, fires and conflict, with an eight-week escalation forecast drawn ahead of the news.

day2.title: Haystacks, End of Summer
day2.why: The same field painted again the next day: Day 2 is not a screen of numbers but the difference between this morning and yesterday — and every figure on it carries its own age.

geo.title: The Rhinoceros
geo.why: A creature drawn from rumour and report, never seen — border posture built from open sources, with the same map played back through time.

sciti.title: The Ideal City
sciti.why: The city the index compares against: 174 urban areas measured against seven pillars, every milestone entered in the ledger in Thai and English.

constitution.title: Moses Smashing the Tablets of the Law
constitution.why: The tablets held up so that they can be read: 279 sections in Thai, English and Chinese, aloud if you want, with the clauses that matter pulled out into study cards.

podcast-20min.title: The Orchestra at the Opera
podcast-20min.why: Twenty minutes, one voice, one room: field notes, city systems, agents and geopolitics, with the question left open at the end of every episode.

ai-council.title: The Last Supper
ai-council.why: Eleven advisers at one table, each with a different prior and a different move: the disagreement is written down, and you leave with a position you can defend.

second-brain.title: Portrait of Erasmus of Rotterdam Writing
second-brain.why: A humanist scholar at his desk annotating texts and linking ideas across volumes: your personal vault wired to every coding platform, notes indexed, and memory preserved.

horizon45.title: Rain, Steam and Speed
horizon45.why: A test, not a survey: real tasks, real attempts, an honest score. The portrait is built from what you did, not from what you said you would do.

ascn.title: Untitled (East Building Mobile)
ascn.collection: National Gallery of Art, Washington, D.C.
ascn.why: One hundred and thirty-four projects across 38 cities, hanging in balance through four review cycles: momentum, not hierarchy.

dao.title: Water Lilies
dao.why: A text read as one surface: 81 chapters in three languages, a study of the characters that carry them, and the colour relationships underneath.

flood-blueprint.title: A Deluge
flood-blueprint.why: Leonardo drew the water to understand it before it came. The blueprint does the same with the system: sensors, drainage, prediction and playbook, laid out for any city to read, fork and adapt.

nonwriter.title: The Arnolfini Portrait
nonwriter.why: The signature on the wall: Jan van Eyck was here. A writer leaves marks — and this one rewrites the draft into the sentence you meant, in your voice, in any language.

drnon-digests.title: Rudolf II as Vertumnus
drnon-digests.why: Many ingredients composed into one face: every morning's lead, what is actually shipping on the AI frontier, and what is only hot air — assembled by hand.

time-pop.title: The Hourglass
time-pop.collection: De Morgan Collection, Cannon Hall Museum
time-pop.why: 261 references with a cited price, a sourced provenance and a credited still — and an honesty ladder that shows exactly where the data refuses to estimate.

openclaw-setup.title: The Hand of God
openclaw-setup.why: A hand pulling form out of rough stone: the machine surveyed, the memory budget checked, the tools risk-tiered, and the runbook written — set-up is the work before the work.

shophouse-metropolis.title: The Shop of Tingqua, the Painter
shophouse-metropolis.why: Live upstairs, workshop on the floor, street through the shutters: 400,000 shophouses, 2,311 of them surveyed, and the reuse argument laid against Treasury land value.

locating-shanghai.title: Along the River During the Qingming Festival (detail)
locating-shanghai.why: The great scroll of a Chinese city in motion, unrolled one section at a time: fifteen chapters, 134 photographs, five hours of audio and 475 citations, read slowly by someone standing in the city.

rag.title: Saint Jerome in His Study
rag.why: A reader inside his own library, every book within reach: your documents cited every time, and when they are silent the answer is 'I don't know'.

each.title: The Moneylender and his Wife
each.why: Gold scales, open ledgers, coins, and records kept in strict balance: ERP, accounting ledgers, cash runway, and double-entry bookkeeping reconciled on one single screen.

colors.title: Colour wheel (Farbenkreis)
colors.why: The first serious attempt to order colour for people rather than for physics: 348 combinations, searchable, each one readable in grayscale, each one copyable as CSS.

axiom-dc.title: The First Six Books of the Elements of Euclid (plate)
axiom-dc.why: Axioms drawn in primary colour: a five-line DNA, tokens, components and an AGENTS.md any agent can read — function first, then subtract.

rams-dc.title: Counter-Composition VI
rams-dc.why: Two layers of the same discipline: a warm-grey field with a hairline grid for one screen, and a closed palette with a disc and a solid arrow for many.

moma-rules.title: Suprematist Composition: White on White
moma-rules.collection: Museum of Modern Art, New York
moma-rules.why: White on white: the rule that a museum will hang almost nothing, if it is exact. Ten laws, a ratchet that fails the build, and a console for what only exists after layout.

o3.title: Market Scene in the Rattanakosin Kingdom
o3.why: Local community commerce, crafts, and produce traded openly: Thailand's 154,078 OTOP registry records across 77 provinces, each carrying its origin, provenance, and maker.

note-1.title: The Peasant Wedding
note-1.why: A working room, mid-task. Nobody is waiting on a committee — the table is laid and the work has already started.

note-2.title: Painter and Female Model in the Atelier (Houwelyck)
note-2.why: One person sets the direction and the other makes the thing. The skill sits in the hand that does not paint.

note-3.title: The Judgement of Solomon
note-3.collection: Original destroyed in 1695; after the workshop picture
note-3.why: The decision comes first. He was asked to settle it, not to gather the evidence before beginning.

note-4.title: The Harvesters
note-4.why: Nobody in the field reports to anybody. The work itself is the hierarchy.

note-5.title: The School of Athens
note-5.why: A room where the argument is the output. Everyone is thinking, and nobody has the last word.

note-6.title: An Experiment on a Bird in the Air Pump
note-6.why: The instrument is in the picture, not in a drawer. You watch the reading being taken.

stack.title: The Art of Painting (detail)
stack.why: One room, one window, everything the work needs inside it. Nothing waits on somebody else.

miaoshen.title: The Bund at Shanghai
miaoshen.why: The Huangpu riverfront and the historical Bund: still water running — the city read by someone standing at the water's edge, written as letters across three languages.

tdv.title: Arch of Constantine in Rome, from Views of Rome
tdv.why: The campus as a working drawing: five buildings, 86,000 square metres, twenty-five published floor plans and one live model — depth, scale and the building as one shape.

page-hero.title: The Deluge
page-hero.why: The water is over the town and it is still dark. Danby painted the flood as something that arrives before anybody is ready for it — the night decides, not the meeting.

page-problem.title: The Battle of Alexander at Issus
page-problem.why: The whole crisis in one picture, seen from a mountain. The two men who have to decide are small figures at the bottom edge of it. The picture is complete and nobody standing inside it can read it.

page-room.title: A Goldsmith in his Shop
page-room.why: The client is at the bench and the bench is where the work happens. No showroom, no office in between — the person who makes the thing is the person you are talking to.

page-step-1.title: The Oath of the Horatii
page-step-1.why: One oath, three swords, and the people who will pay for it. Week one is not about collecting requirements — it is about naming one decision, the person who owns it, and what it costs to be wrong in time.

page-step-2.title: The Alchemist Discovering Phosphorus
page-step-2.why: The apparatus on the bench is built from what the room already had. The glow either shows up in front of everybody or it does not — no procurement, no lead time, no promise.

page-step-3.title: The Lacemaker
page-step-3.why: One hook, one thread, the whole work in her hands. Every screen is instrumented from day one — who opens it, which decision it served — and the next version is built from what the first one taught.

page-changed.title: The Gross Clinic
page-changed.why: The operation, live, with the wound open and nothing tidied away. A first screen is one decision on real data, shown while it is still rough — not a finished product, and not sold as one.

page-questions.title: Christ and the Woman Taken in Adultery (detail)
page-questions.why: The question is put in front of everybody, and the answer comes from the one person who can give it. Cost, data, safety, the team, what outlives the launch — bring them to the room, not to a form.

page-catalogue.title: Interior of a Picture Gallery with the Collection of Cardinal Silvio Valenti Gonzaga
page-catalogue.why: A hall where every picture is framed, hung and named, with people in the middle of it deciding what to look at next. That is this book: one plate per system, marked live or not live.

bangkok-ioc.title: Akasaka: Inn with Serving Maids, from The Fifty-three Stations of the Tōkaidō
bangkok-ioc.collection: Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York
bangkok-ioc.why: A station is a place to stay before it is anything else: an inn, a price, the road you walk in the morning. Hiroshige drew the Tōkaidō as fifty-three of them, each judged by who is in the room. Six BTS station areas read the same way — your own limits first, then what is actually around the platform.

life.title: The Steps of Life (Trap des Levens)
life.why: A whole life counted in steps of ten: up to fifty, down to a hundred, one figure on every age and a verse beneath each. Life plays the same stair at 2× to 20×, and at every step a fork with a cost.

burma.artist: Court of King Mindon or Thibaw Workshops
burma.title: Accordion-Fold Paper Manuscript (Burmese Parabaik)
burma.collection: Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York
burma.why: The folding parabaik of the Konbaung court unfolded into continuous narrative panels: persistent rooms, daily community chronicles, and Burmese prose preserved across generations.
burma.medium: watercolor and gold on mulberry paper

llm.title: An Iron Forge
llm.why: Raw iron shaped under the water-hammer into a tool you can hold: organization-specific intelligence forged directly from private records into an open model weight.

mean.artist: Unknown maker; photograph by Donald Macbeth
mean.title: The Rosetta Stone
mean.why: One text in two languages and three scripts: meaning recovered through comparison. A personal lexicon likewise asks what a word means across the languages and experiences of its author.

ninja.title: The Knifegrinder (El Afilador)
ninja.why: A practitioner, a modest tool, a concrete service. Ninja Innovation argues for the same order: understand the person and the problem, then choose the smallest useful means.

slowdown.title: The House of Cards
slowdown.why: A structure that only holds if each move receives attention. Pausing, looking, and placing carefully are the activity in the picture, and the discipline this book asks its reader to practise.

dhaka.title: Part of the Interior of the City of Dacca
dhaka.why: A nineteenth-century view of Dhaka centering on the Purana Qila and the water gate built to monitor and withstand monsoon inundation. DHKx records Dhaka block by block with modern 3D topography to read urban density and water flows where memory and water meet.

tsunami.title: The Life Line
tsunami.why: A breeches buoy suspends a rescue between drowning waves and shore safety, the operator hidden behind drenched oilskins while the apparatus performs its mechanical duty. Soonami operates as that lifeline along the Andaman rim, giving coastal emergency teams the critical seconds before the surge arrives.

universe-69.title: The Creation of the World (The Garden of Earthly Delights exterior shutters)
universe-69.why: Bosch renders the world as a fragile, translucent sphere floating in silent space, an intact biosphere observed from the exterior by its creator without active interference. Universe 69 operates on the exact same premise: two sealed procedural worlds observed continuously, governed by deterministic mechanics, and never helped.

dog.title: White Poodle in a Punt
dog.why: Stubbs observed animal anatomy and character with scientific rigor, depicting a dog poised attentively aboard a small river craft. CANINE applies procedural 3D modeling and biological proportioning to capture the form, gait, and alert posture of Thailand's native Bangkaew.

pavilion.title: Proun 99
pavilion.collection: Yale University Art Gallery, New Haven
pavilion.why: Lissitzky conceived Proun as the station where painting shifts into three-dimensional architecture, constructing weightless spatial forms from fundamental geometric materials without historical baggage. The Pavilion applies this exact modern architectural discipline to the open web: constructing a zero-cost, browser-native spatial world from scratch with steel, travertine, and glass, liberating virtual environments from hyperscaler data silos and proprietary extraction.
pavilion.medium: water soluble and metallic paint on wood

100days.title: The Rongxi Studio
100days.why: Ni Zan depicts an empty pavilion by quiet water, stripped of ornament, surrounded by sparse trees and distant hills. 'Rongxi' means a room barely large enough to hold one's knees: the quintessential statement of deliberate quiet, wandering, and a small life carefully lived in solitude.
